title: Tenali Raman and the Stone That Wept Oil

full_text:
Outside the southern gates of Vijayanagara, a cunning ascetic named Swami Prakashananda set up an altar around an ordinary black basalt stone.
He proclaimed to gathering crowds of pilgrims:
'Behold the Miraculous Weeping Stone of Agastya!
Whenever I chant my sacred morning mantras, this holy stone miraculously weeps fragrant sesame oil from its pores!
Whoever donates a gold coin shall receive a drop of this miraculous oil to cure all diseases!'

Hundreds of sick pilgrims and poor villagers donated their hard-earned coins, and indeed, every morning at sunrise, glistening drops of golden oil seeped from the crevices of the black basalt rock!
The municipal councilors were awed, urging the King to build a grand gold-plated temple over the stone.

Tenali Raman visited the site at dusk after the pilgrims had departed.
He observed that the stone was black basalt—a dense, non-porous volcanic rock that cannot absorb or weep oil naturally.
Tenali examined the earthen hillock directly behind the stone altar:
He noticed that the grass was recently planted, and an ancient hollow tamarind tree stood ten paces behind the rock.

That night, accompanied by two trusted guards with spades, Tenali dug into the hillock behind the basalt stone.
Just two feet beneath the surface, they uncovered a hidden lead pipe running from the hollow trunk of the tamarind tree directly into a concealed drilled hole in the back of the basalt stone!
Tenali climbed the tamarind tree:
Inside the hollow trunk was a large copper tank filled with thirty gallons of sesame oil, fitted with a brass valve that could be turned on from behind the tree!

Tenali smiled. He did not break the pipe.
Instead, he poured a bottle of dark, foul-smelling fish oil and crushed bitter neem juice into the copper tank!

The next morning, Swami Prakashananda assembled hundreds of pilgrims, King Krishnadevaraya, and the ministers.
The ascetic began chanting loudly, while his hidden disciple turned the valve behind the tree!
The stone began to 'weep' oil!

The ascetic proudly caught the first drops in a silver spoon and offered it to the King:
'Taste the celestial nectar, Your Majesty!'
The moment the King smelled the spoon, a nauseating stench of rotten fish and bitter neem filled the air!
The King gagged in disgust:
'Ugh! What foul devil's stench is this?'

Tenali Raman stepped out from behind the tamarind tree, holding the severed lead pipe and the copper tank:
'Behold the source of the miracle, Maharaj!
The ascetic’s stone weeps whatever oil is poured into his secret tank!
Yesterday it wept sweet sesame oil to fleece the poor; today it weeps rotten fish to reveal the stench of his fraud!'

The crowd gasped in outrage.
The King ordered the charlatan arrested and sentenced to clean the public sewage canals for a year, while Tenali showed that superstitious miracles dissolve when their plumbing is exposed.
moral: Supernatural hoaxes that fake divine miracles to extract donations are demolished by simple inspection.
